A 19th-century map illustration of the Bight of Benin showing Lagos island, the lagoon, Badagry, and Epe. Two distinct points should be marked: "1851: Bombardment (Kosoko ousted)" and "1861: Annexation (Dosunmu cedes Lagos)". A small drawing of British naval ships offshore. Style: clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

An illustration showing two contrasting scenes of conquest methods. On the left, a British agent in colonial dress sitting with a local chief, both pointing at a piece of paper on a table (Treaty). On the right, a British gunboat on a river with its cannons pointed towards a coastal settlement (Gunboat Diplomacy).

A flow chart titled "Results of the British Conquest". The main box "British Conquest" splits into three branches. Branch 1: "Political" pointing to "Loss of Sovereignty", "Colonial Administration", "Indirect Rule". Branch 2: "Economic" pointing to "Cash Crop Economy", "New Currency & Taxes", "Railways Built". Branch 3: "Social" pointing to "Spread of Western Education", "End of Internal Slavery", "Urbanization".
